stories.title: OpenAI's chief scientist proposes an industry speed limit on AI measured by perplexity

articles.title: OpenAI's chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development

facts.text: In this post, I argue for establishing perplexity (or, equivalently, cross-entropy loss) as a metric to compare between model developers and inform shared safety standards.
Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token on average; lower perplexity means better predictions.
GPT‑4, at ~0.91, was proficient at utilizing chain-of-thought reasoning productively
Now, as we have reached losses below 0.8, we have seen the emergence of transformative capabilities in fields like cybersecurity and mathematics.

I further propose common limits, based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone
Publishing our internal perplexity measurements took some consideration; it gives competitors a clearer picture of where we stand
Pachocki’s post — described by Altman as “the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while”
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei then published a plan to “pace the frontier,” seemingly endorsed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.
Perplexity as a shared metric has challenges: Difficulty of comparison across labs.

stories.notes: Original company post read in full. Also in Reuters (Technology) and AI타임스, ZDNet Korea feeds. Pairs with Hendrycks pause story; pick only one. Strong evening-agnostic global story, morning slot fine.

facts.text: Der technologielastige Börsenindex Nasdaq 100 verlor im Wochenverlauf 10,4 Prozent seiner Punkte, der breiter aufgestellte S&P 500 kam mit 8,6 Prozent Wochenminus nicht viel besser weg.

Das ... ließ die Nvidia-Aktie diesen Monat um 39 Prozent absacken.
Wie die Nachrichtenagentur Reuters am Freitag berichtete, ermitteln die US-Börsenaufseher bei Nvidia. ... Nach dem Bekanntwerden schloss die Aktie am Freitag mit 14 Prozent im Minus.
Taiex, der Börsenindex für Unternehmen, die an der taiwanesischen Börse gehandelt werden, verlor diese Woche 17,5 Prozent.
Bloomberg und Financial Times sprechen in Bezug auf den Nasdaq 100 inzwischen von einem Bärenmarkt – als Beleg sehen sie den Kursverlust von 20 Prozent seit dem jüngsten Hoch im Oktober.
Eine Ermittlung allein ist noch kein Indikator für Fehlverhalten. (what exactly is investigated was not disclosed; Nvidia declined to comment)
Statt der großen KI-Euphorie ... steht nun die Frage im Raum, ob KI-Hersteller zu viel Geld ausgeben und leihen, um am Ende noch profitabel zu sein.

articles.title: Signal restricts mobile screenshots as it confronts ‘existential threat’ of AI surveillance

facts.text: Signal announced Friday that it’s limiting users’ ability to take screenshots within the secure messaging app
a response to what President Meredith Whittaker described as the “existential threat” of operating systems that integrate agentic AI.
by giving AI agents the ability to “scan” the information on users’ screens, Windows, Android, and macOS/iOS “are undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy.”
your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment
Signal already sought to limit these risks by blocking screenshots of its Windows app by default. Now it’s adding similar restrictions in Android and iOS.
users can disable this setting if they wish, which Whittaker said would “break our privacy guarantees.”
She also admitted this is an “incomplete” solution

stories.notes: Der Standard (Austria) also covers it (page paywalled/consent wall, only intro read). Good reader-impact and Europe-angle story.

stories.title: Anthropic mathematician claims Claude helped prove the Riemann hypothesis
stories.repeat_note: Anthropic IPO covered 2026-11-19 (anthropic-ant-debut); Riemann only mentioned in 11-22 briefs as a side note. Different angle but same company.

articles.title: Anthropic researcher claims Riemann proof with Claude

facts.text: Mmathematician at Anthropic says he has used the company’s Claude AI model to prove the Riemann hypothesis (Levent Alpöge, note on his website on Friday, Bloomberg reported).
“I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Alpöge wrote.
The hypothesis, first proposed in 1859, concerns how prime numbers are spread out. It is one of the Clay Mathematics Institute’s seven Millennium Prize Problems, each of which carries a $1m prize.
The code runs to about 17 million lines, Science reported. (proof released in Lean)
Andrew Sutherland, a senior research scientist at MIT, told Bloomberg he had checked the code on his own computer.
Kevin Buzzard, a professor at Imperial College London, said nobody yet understands what the proof shows, Al Jazeera reported. The proof has not been formally accepted.
The claim came a day after the company’s record stock market debut.
In September, OpenAI said its models had produced a solution to the Navier-Stokes problem.

stories.notes: Secondhand (TNW citing Bloomberg, Science, SciAm, Al Jazeera). Must say 'claims'. Also covered by SCMP (200th birthday event in China, 16:01Z) and TechCrunch headline 'AI claimed a solution ... and a human did, too' - neither read. Carried over from 11-21/11-22 backlog as unverified; now has MIT check.

stories.title: Google retires the Nest app in January and the Google Assistant on speakers in August 2027, switching smart homes to Gemini

articles.title: Google integriert Nest-Geräte in Home-App und wechselt im Smart Home zu Gemini

facts.text: Im August 2027 wird der Google Assistant für Lautsprecher und smarte Displays endgültig durch den Sprachassistenten Gemini for Home ersetzt.
Bereits im Januar wird die Nest-App eingestellt. Alle bisherigen Nest-Geräte werden dann über Googles Home-App gesteuert.
Wer seine Nest-Geräte noch damit bedient, muss bis zum 25. Januar 2027 auf Googles Home-App umsteigen
Auf Mobilgeräten wurde der Google Assistant bereits im September endgültig abgeschaltet.
Abonnements von Nest Aware wechseln Ende Januar ebenfalls automatisch – zu Google Home Premium.
Zu den 20 unterstützten Ländern gehören auch Deutschland, Österreich und die Schweiz.
Nutzer sollten lediglich individuelle Videoclips herunterladen, die mit der Nest-App möglicherweise gesichert wurden.

stories.repeat_note: Carried from 2026-11-22 runner-ups (#1). Related theme to perplexity story (both OpenAI) - choose one.

articles.title: OpenAI research agents cost $2,400 a day per researcher, report says

facts.text: OpenAI says its coding agents now complete 46% of research tasks that would take a person two to four hours, with no human help. In March the figure was 23%.
The figures come from Research acceleration: The jagged frontier, a report OpenAI published on Wednesday.
the median OpenAI researcher used about $2,400 of agent time a day in October. That is up 62% from $1,500 in September.
agent use per researcher rose elevenfold, from 0.5 to 5.7 “agent workdays” a day.
Agents succeeded alone 79% of the time when monitoring training runs ... They managed 25% when writing code for inference and serving systems
OpenAI flags a caveat in its own numbers. As agents improved, researchers may have changed which tasks they handed over
In a survey of 101 research staff ... The median answer was 40% of team headcount, or 30% of team compute.
OpenAI says labs should be required to track and publicly report signs of recursive self-improvement

stories.notes: Secondhand: OpenAI's own report was not read; TNW is the readable source. Cite as TNW reporting OpenAI's report.

stories.title: Dan Hendrycks calls for an indefinite pause on frontier AI training at DealBook; Neuralink co-founder says it would need a surveillance state

articles.title: DealBook AGI panel: Dan Hendrycks wants frontier AI training paused

facts.text: Dan Hendrycks used the DealBook Summit to call for an indefinite pause on frontier AI training runs. Max Hodak, on the same panel, said enforcing one would take a surveillance state.
Hendrycks runs the Center for AI Safety
Hodak co-founded Neuralink and now runs Science Corporation.
“So now it’s, we’re going to need a more blunt intervention. That’s how it is,” Hendrycks said.
He described an indefinite pause on the biggest training runs, with carve-outs for narrow models such as DeepMind’s AlphaFold and voice models. Labs could still sell inference
“You’re setting up like an exhaustive surveillance state on the internet to enforce this,” Hodak said.
Staniszewski agreed a pause could work with global alignment, but said whether anyone can get it “is the big question mark”.
Hendrycks repeated the charges of the statement his group organised against the company [Anthropic]

stories.notes: Panel happened Wednesday (18 Nov); TNW report 21 Nov, so a bit stale. Best used as context inside the OpenAI speed-limit story.

stories.title: Etsy will rewrite new AI-training terms after sellers close their shops

articles.title: Etsy AI terms prompt sellers to close shops as Etsy promises a rewrite

facts.text: Etsy says it will revise its new terms of use. Longtime sellers had begun closing their shops over a clause that lets it use their work to train AI.
The new terms take effect on 16 December.
Etsy and its “third party partners and vendors” may use sellers’ content to “develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies.”
The previous version had no clause about AI, the Times reported.
Etsy will not “use your content to train A.I. models designed to copy your original work or replace your creativity,” Ossman wrote.
In 2022, more than 20,000 sellers went on strike over a fee rise.
Illustrator Aaron Millard said on Instagram he was deleting the shop he had run for nearly a decade. He wrote that sellers had no way to opt out.

stories.notes: Secondhand (TNW citing New York Times). Revised wording not yet published.

articles.title: Fear of wearable devices spreads beyond education sector

facts.text: Samsung Electronics requires camera-covering stickers on smart glasses brought onto its premises, while SK hynix, Hyundai Motor and LG Group have introduced restrictions or screening measures.
The Defense Ministry’s directive took effect Nov. 1 and applies to military personnel and outside visitors.
Hyundai Motor requires outside visitors to its Seoul headquarters, research centers and factories to declare and obtain approval for AI wearables.
At military facilities without X-ray equipment, security personnel can inspect glasses for camera lenses, LEDs, charging contacts, control buttons and unusually thick frames.
Unlike smartphones, which can be easily identified and restricted, smart glasses can look almost identical to conventional eyewear while continuously collecting images and audio.
